died-at:jesus_905>jerusalem_636@2251fc.note: Matthew 16:21 says he must go to Jerusalem to be killed; the crucifixion site (27:33) is not named as the city, so the location is a reading.

member-of:mary_1938>tribe-of-judah@2918b.note: Mary's tribe is not stated. It follows only if Heli (3:23) is her father, which Luke does not say; Luke's line runs to Juda (3:33).

occurred-at:an-angel-speaks-to-joseph-in.note: Matthew places Joseph's dreams in Egypt (2:19) and before the move to Galilee (2:22), not at Nazareth; the dream of 2:22 comes before he dwelt there (2:23).

occurred-at:fig-tree-cursed>olivet_907@5.note: Matthew names the Mount of Olives only at 21:1; the cursing is on the road from Bethany (21:17-18). That Bethany lies on Olivet is outside the text.

occurred-at:feeding-of-four-thousand>dec.note: Matthew 15:29 puts the feeding by the Sea of Galilee and 15:39 in the coasts of Magdala; Mark 8:10 says Dalmanutha. Decapolis is not named.

occurred-at:healing-a-boy-with-a-demon>m.note: Matthew 17:1 says only 'an high mountain apart'; the boy is healed after they come down to the crowd (17:14-18). Naming it Mount Hermon is an outside identification.

occurred-at:healing-a-withered-hand>cape.note: Mark 2:1 has him in Capernaum; 3:1 says he 'entered again into the synagogue' without naming it, so Capernaum comes from 1:21 by inference.

occurred-at:jesus-meets-martha-and-mary>.note: Luke 10:38 names only 'a certain village'; John 11:1 places Martha and Mary in Bethany, so equating the village with Bethany is a reading.

occurred-at:judas-plans-betrayal>jerusal.note: Matthew names no city for the plot; 26:3 gives the high priest's palace and 26:18 'the city' for the passover, so Jerusalem is a reading.

occurred-at:resurrection-and-ascension>m.note: Acts 1:9 has him taken up from the disciples, and 1:12 says they returned from the mount called Olivet.

occurred-at:resurrection-and-ascension>s.note: John 21:1 places an appearance at the sea of Tiberias, and John 6:1 says that is the sea of Galilee.

occurred-at:teaching-by-the-fig-tree>oli.note: Matthew 24:3 has Jesus sitting on the mount of Olives, and 24:32 gives the parable of the fig tree.

occurred-at:the-transfiguation>mount_her.note: Matthew 17:1-2 says only 'an high mountain apart'; Mount Hermon is an outside identification.

parent-of:heli_1484>mary_1938@063a3c.note: Luke 3:23 makes Heli the father of Joseph, Mary's husband (matt.1.16); Heli as Mary's own father is an outside identification.

parent-of:herod_1504>herod_1505@a9486e.note: Matthew 2:1 and 14:1 name two Herods, but no father-son link is stated; the parentage is outside history.

parent-of:herod_1504>philip_2345@ccf367.note: Matthew 14:3 and Luke 3:1 call a Philip Herod's brother without naming their father; which Philip this key is also goes beyond the text.

parent-of:herod_1504>philip_2346@c9f363.note: Matthew 14:3 and Luke 3:1 call a Philip Herod's brother without naming their father; which Philip this key is also goes beyond the text.

parent-of:joseph_1715>jude_1756@c76bd0.note: Matthew 1:25 implies later sons of Mary and Joseph, and 13:55 names Judas among Jesus' brethren; Joseph as Jude's father is an inference. Luke 3:30 is another Joseph.

part-of:abilene_12>aram_82@d88be8.note: Luke 3:1 names Abilene and Matthew 4:24 names Syria; that Abilene lay within Aram (Syria) is outside geography.

part-of:cana_271>asher_1287@cea20d.note: John 2:1 places Cana in Galilee; Joshua 19:28 lists Kanah in Asher's lot. Equating the two is an identification from outside the text.

part-of:tiberias_1161>naphtali_1284@b1d6.note: John 6:1 names the sea of Tiberias; Joshua 19:35 lists Hammath in Naphtali. Hammath as Tiberias is an outside identification.

participated-in:jesus_905>childhood-of-j.note: Jesus is the child the events concern: born (2:7), growing (2:40), taken up to the temple at twelve (2:42).

participated-in:jesus_905>crucifixion-an.note: Jesus is crucified (27:35), yields up the ghost (27:50), and is laid in Joseph's tomb (27:60).

participated-in:jesus_905>discourse-with.note: The Pharisees and Sadducees come tempting him for a sign (16:1); he answers them (16:2) and warns of their leaven (16:6).

participated-in:jesus_905>jesus-2nd-tour.note: Matthew 9:35 has Jesus touring all the cities and villages, teaching and healing; calling it the second tour relies on an outside harmony.

participated-in:jesus_905>jesus-rejected.note: He stands up to read (4:16), speaks (4:22), and is thrust out of the city by the synagogue crowd (4:28-29).

participated-in:jesus_905>mustard-seed-a.note: Jesus gives the parables of the mustard seed and the leaven (13:18-21).

participated-in:jesus_905>temple-present.note: The parents bring the child to Jerusalem (2:22), and Simeon takes him up in his arms (2:27-28).

participated-in:peter_2745>roman-trials@.note: Peter is in the high priest's court (john.18.15-18, 25-27) while Jesus is before Pilate (john.18.28-38), and Peter is not named there.

participated-in:peter_2745>woes-and-para.note: Peter asks at 12:41 in a discourse opened by a warning about the Pharisees (12:1); the Pharisees' woes at 11:37-54 do not name him.

visited:andrew_264>jerusalem_636@97ea41.note: Andrew asks Jesus privately with Peter, James and John (13:3), while they sit on Olivet over against the temple (13:1-3).

visited:james_719>jerusalem_636@635736.note: Paul went up to Jerusalem to see Peter (1:18) and saw no other apostle save James the Lord's brother (1:19).

visited:mary_1938>jerusalem_636@3da90e.note: Mary goes up with Joseph to Jerusalem (2:22, 2:42) and seeks Jesus there, saying 'thy father and I have sought thee' (2:48).

visited:satan_2476>jerusalem_636@7906f2.note: The devil takes Jesus to Jerusalem and sets him on the temple pinnacle (Luke 4:9); Matthew 4:5 calls it the holy city.
